name: EXP-CLI-001 Decompose the CLI monolith behind a lazy dispatcher
goal:
The CLI is one 9163-line file that loads 2.27 MB of framework before it can answer any question, and the
test suite pays that 758 times. Decompose it behind a lazy dispatcher. This is the prerequisite for the
testing work, not a parallel track: a suite that spawns an unusable monolith cannot be made cheap by
scheduling, merging or selecting around it.

MEASURED COST (2026-10-13, branch arena/841cc45d-synth, 2-core sandbox, median of 7 runs, real repo with a
452-event ledger)

  node -e '1'                            25.2 ms   process floor
  entry.js  --version   (LIGHT path)    100.1 ms   145 modules /  964 KB loaded eagerly
  synth.js  --version   (MONOLITH)      175.7 ms   296 modules / 2272 KB loaded eagerly
  entry.js  status                      231.2 ms
  synth.js  status                      276.8 ms
  entry.js  explain replay              140.1 ms    45 modules /  154 KB  <- what "light" should look like
  entry.js  expedition list             308.4 ms   (falls through to the monolith)
  synth.js  expedition list             305.2 ms

  import-only cost: sdk/paths/index.js 34.8 ms (10 modules/16 KB), infra/index.js 50.2 ms,
  status-light.js 91.0 ms (134 modules/916 KB), core/bootstrap.js 104.7 ms (170 modules/1091 KB)

  CPU profile of a single invocation: compileSourceTextModule 53.4 ms (--version), 40.4 ms (status),
  55.7 ms (verify); plus getPackageScopeConfig 9.1 ms, internalModuleStat 6.5 ms, realpathSync /
  resolvePackageTargetString / #cachedDefaultResolve, and 11.9-18.2 ms of GC. Module loading and ESM
  resolution - which scale with module COUNT - are 60-70% of a trivial verb and 25-33% of a real one.

So printing a version string costs 150 ms of framework loading through the monolith and 75 ms through the
dispatcher. The command itself is the cheap part.

THE LIGHT PATH IS NOT LIGHT. src/cli/entry.ts (129 lines) already has the right shape: LIGHT_COMMANDS =
{version, --version, -v, help, --help, -h, status} served without importing synth.js, per-verb
`await import()` for explain identity / resume / governance, then `const { main } = await import("./synth.js")`
for everything else. But it statically imports status-light.js, which pulls 134 modules / 916 KB - 45% of the
monolith's graph. explain-replay-light.js (45 modules) and explain-flags.js (1 module) prove the pattern works
when the module is actually narrow. The seam exists; it was just never carried below synth.ts.

WHY IT BLOCKS THE TESTING WORK
  * tests/helpers/cli-harness.js:24 sets CLI_PATH = dist/cli/synth.js and spawns THAT, so all 106 spawning
    suites bypass the dispatcher and pay the monolith on every call.
  * 758 CLI-spawn call-sites across 106 of 242 test files (623 runSynth, 53 spawnSync, 45 runCli,
    35 execFileSync, 2 createExecRunner) - a LOWER bound, since call-sites inside loops run many times.
    At the measured 176-305 ms per call that is roughly 2.5 minutes of the 8m20s full serial suite spent
    re-loading the same 2.27 MB, over and over, to run a verb that needs 16 KB of it.
  * This is why merging suites (EXP-TEST-002) and scheduling them (EXP-TEST-003) cannot fix the cost: both
    change how many processes run, not what each process loads. Per-process cost is the dominant term.

THE MONOLITH'S SHAPE (the decomposition seams)
  * src/cli/synth.ts: 9163 lines / 352 KB source; dist/cli/synth.js 8101 lines / 357 KB
  * 97 cmd* handlers plus 85 non-cmd top-level helpers = 182 top-level functions in one file
  * 70 static imports resolving to 633 KB of source, against 9 dynamic imports in synth.ts (16 across src/cli)
  * the 85 helpers are already cohesive clusters, which is where extraction starts:
      git / working tree: getWorkingTreeStatus, isWorkingTreeDirty, runGitSpawn, getUntrackedSourcePaths,
        existingAutoCommitPathspecs, isTrackedPath, isScratchFile, isNonSourcePath,
        getNonDerivedWorkingTreeStatus, collectDerivedStateFiles, isAutoCommitEnabled
      ceremony / auto-commit: markCeremony, installExitFlush, flushPendingCeremony,
        wrapHandleIntentWithCeremony, bootstrapWithCapabilities
      gates: gateDecision, printGateBlock
      telemetry / args: setAgentTelemetryFromFlags, parseArgs
  * largest modules loaded eagerly but not needed by the light path: synth.js 357 KB,
    explain-observability.js 41 KB, first-contact.js 40 KB, control/execution-gate.js 38 KB,
    discovery/projections/project-model-capability.js 33 KB, state/derived/build-derived-state.js 27 KB

WHAT GOOD LOOKS LIKE
A thin dispatcher that knows verb names and how to load them, and nothing else. Handler modules grouped by
namespace (mission, expedition, ledger deliver/seal, explain, first-contact, task, repo, adapter,
doctor/checkpoint, log, validate, governance). Shared helper clusters extracted ONCE into modules of their
own, so handlers move without duplicating them. entry.ts keeps LIGHT_COMMANDS and status-light becomes
genuinely light. dist/cli/synth.js stays as a compatibility entry with identical behaviour, so nothing that
spawns it today breaks.

PROPOSED BUDGETS (measured, median of >=7, core count recorded, in both a real-ledger and an empty project)
  * synth --version        <=  45 ms   (from 100 light / 176 monolith)
  * synth status           <= 130 ms   (from 231 / 277)
  * synth explain replay   <= 110 ms   (from 140)
  * dispatcher eager graph <=  25 modules / <= 150 KB   (from 145 / 964)
  * no verb loads more than 40% of the total module graph unless its work genuinely requires it
  * a DERIVED guard test that recomputes the eager graph per entry point and re-measures the representative
    verbs, failing on regression - so re-monolithization is caught by a number, not by a review.

PHASES (each independently measurable and revertible)
  1. Audit module-load-time side effects BEFORE making anything lazy, then extract the helper clusters.
  2. Slim status-light.js; re-measure the dispatcher graph.
  3. Turn synth.ts dispatch into a verb -> loader registry with per-namespace dynamic imports.
  4. Point tests/helpers/cli-harness.js at the dispatcher; keep synth.js compatible.
  5. Add the load-budget guard; re-baseline dist-manifest / determinism / proof.

RISKS, NAMED
  * Import-time capture: module-level constants bound to process.cwd() at load (EVENT_LOG_FILE and
    EVENT_STREAM_DIR in src/infra/event-store.ts are exactly this). Lazy loading changes WHEN a module is
    first imported, so any verb that resolves roots or changes cwd later could observe different values.
    Phase 1 audits every module-load-time capture; this is the main correctness hazard, not the line count.
  * Observable behaviour must not move: exit codes, stderr, JSON envelopes and the exact detail strings.
    758 spawn call-sites assert on them, and expedition 2c9c6c62's guarantees (truthful log/checkpoint/
    doctor, `skipped` never counted as pass) must survive verbatim.
  * Four files reference src/cli/synth.ts BY PATH and must move with the code, never be deleted:
    tests/verify-engine.test.js (the guard added by 2c9c6c62 asserting synth.ts imports locateEventLog and
    contains no legacy-only presence test), tests/artifact-policy.test.js, tests/governance-orchestration.test.js,
    tests/impact-analyzer.test.js.
  * dist-manifest.json (1044 files, rootHash 13e1948b...) and the determinism/proof checks change when files
    are added; re-baseline deliberately and say so in the evidence.
  * Circular imports: synth.ts's 70 static imports include modules that reach back into cli/.

NON-GOALS
  * No behaviour, flag, output or verb-surface changes. No new verbs.
  * Not the test inventory or file-ownership guard (EXP-TEST-005, 74c33996d5e7cf32), not suite merging
    (EXP-TEST-002), not the sharded runner (EXP-TEST-003), not the logging/failure envelope (EXP-TEST-001),
    not explicit-environment fields (EXP-TEST-004).
  * Not shrinking core/bootstrap.js (170 modules / 1091 KB, 13 eager steps). This expedition makes it lazily
    REACHABLE so only verbs that need it pay for it; making it smaller is a separate lever.
  * Not fixing the 37 red orphan suites (draft 03f9134a5ecbde03 and EXP-TEST-005).

ACCEPTANCE
  * The budgets above are met, with the measurement method and core count recorded as evidence.
  * Eager graph per entry point is measured and recorded; the dispatcher is <= 25 modules.
  * `npm run test:all` stays green (127 files, 5m34s today) and no currently-green orphan turns red.
  * All 758 spawn call-sites pass unchanged; the only test edits are the harness path and the four
    source-path guards that move with the code.
  * The load-budget guard fails when a handler is added to the dispatcher's eager graph (proved by a
    deliberate temporary regression in the test, then removed).
  * `synth verify` ok, and `synth log` / `checkpoint` / `doctor` still report real counts and layouts on this
    repository.

SEQUENCING (operator decision, 2026-10-13): this runs BEFORE the testing-strategy work. After it lands,
EXP-TEST-002's merge arithmetic and EXP-TEST-003's speedup measurements must be re-taken, because the
per-process term they were implicitly optimizing changes by roughly 3x.
